newsitem.title: USA: Jet fuel trade dries up as American strike looms.
newsitem.headline: Jet fuel trade dries up as American strike looms.

text.p: Spot jet fuel trading ground to a halt Friday afternoon as the deadline for the American Airline pilots' strike crept nearer.
buyers, expecting prices to drop in the event of a strike, took to the sidelines, though sellers attempted to boost spot market differentials in the U.S. Gulf (USG)
"People aren't climbing over each other to get things done," one spot market player said. "There's talk, but there's no market here."

American's pilots union said Friday it was not optimistic about averting a strike, though a government mediator said he was somewhat more encouraged by the talks. The pilots have set a midnight deadline for an agreement to avert a strike.
American Airlines buys 130,000 to 140,000 barrels per day of jet fuel in the U.S., nearly 10 percent of the total U.S. demand.

Without the demand from American, the nation's second largest airline, traders said jet fuel prices will likely sag, although some argued the market may not see the downward pressure unless a strike lasts for more than a few days.

"American started cutting back on supplies about a month ago," another trader said, so there may be little immediate bearish movement because American's absence may already be factored into current prices.
"A price drop may not begin for four or five days," the trader added.
USG 54-grade jet fuel for delivery on the back fourth cycle of the Colonial Pipeline was offered at 4.00 cents over the NYMEX price, up about 0.50 cent from Thursday.
However, traders said very few buyers were evident -- with activity further depressed by the approach of the long Presidents Day weekend -- and none appeared interested in those offers.
Offers for USG 54-grade barrels for late February delivery also firmed to about 1.75 cents over the NYMEX, although no trades were reported.
New York Harbor 54-grade jet fuel was talked on either side of 5.50 cents over the screen, about 0.25 cent down from Thursday.
